text:
The Lagos State Police Command has detained an Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP), Omotayo Olajide, following the death of a young girl during a shooting incident in the Nosamu area of Ajegunle, Lagos.
The incident, which occurred between 9.30pm and 10pm on Thursday, November 5, 2026, also left another girl injured.
The deceased, identified as Omole Taiwo, reportedly died from gunshot injuries after being rushed to the hospital, while the second victim is receiving medical attention and said to be in stable condition.
Tension had gripped Ajegunle, in the Ajeromi-Ifelodun Local Government Area of Lagos State, following the alleged shooting of two children by the ASP, resulting in the death of a two-year-old girl.
The toddler was said to have died from bullet wounds sustained during the incident, while another victim is currently receiving medical attention at an undisclosed hospital after sustaining gunshot injuries.
The incident, which reportedly involved a police officer attached to the Ajeromi Police Station, was suspected to have been under the influence of alcohol.
But the command, in a statement issued on Saturday by its spokesperson, SP Abimbola Adebisi, disclosed that the officer was immediately disarmed and detained, while the State Criminal Investigation Department had taken over the matter.
According to Adebisi, preliminary findings revealed that Olajide and other officers were deployed to the area following a distress call over a violent clash between two rival groups, identified as Nosamu Boys and Alayabiagba Boys, reportedly fighting over toll collection.
“The groups were said to have been armed with cutlasses and other dangerous weapons when the police team arrived,” the Command’s Spokesperson said.
Explaining how the incident occurred, Adebisi revealed that during the operation, ASP Olajide discharged his firearm, and the bullet struck the two girls.
“Both victims were initially rushed to Ajeromi General Hospital, but the deceased was subsequently transferred to the Lagos State University Teaching Hospital (LASUTH), Ikeja, where she later died,” she said.
While expressing his sadness over the incident, the State Commissioner of Police, CP Tijani Fatai, said the officer’s detention and transfer of the case to the SCID were aimed at ensuring a thorough and impartial investigation.
He added that the investigation would establish the circumstances surrounding the shooting and determine the appropriate legal and disciplinary action.
Fatai, who also visited the bereaved family to offer his condolences, assured them that justice would be served.
He vowed that no officer found culpable would be shielded, reaffirming the command’s commitment to the protection of lives, professionalism and accountability.
He, however, urged members of the public with useful information about the incident to report to the nearest police station or the command’s Public Relations Department.
